newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Scania says Europe market share 15.8 pct Jan-April.
newsitem.headline: Scania says Europe market share 15.8 pct Jan-April.

text.p: Swedish truck and bus maker Scania said on Wednesday its market share in Europe in the first four months of the year totalled 15.8 percent.
The company also said figures for April indicated a 14 percent downturn on the total European truck market for 1997. The company said prices on the European market were nearing their bottom.
The head of Scania's marketing for Europe, Urban Erdtman, told Reuters the figure for market share represented an increase over the same 1996 period.
"We have taken market share that we lost earlier," Erdtman said. He said price pressure was easing but was not especially optimistic about this year.
"There is still a lot of pressure on prices in Europe but I think we are near the bottom. But I would not count on rising prices in 1997," he said.
"In the first four months the official registrations in Europe indicate a 14 percent fall compared to the same 1996 period," Erdtman said.
"The pace in the first quarter points to a total market of 150,000 (for 1997)," he said.
